title: What is an agent with tools?

beats.narration: An AI agent works like an office with two people.
beats.on_screen: Illustration: an office. An assistant at a desk with a pile of mail; a clerk beside a filing cabinet and a post room.

beats.narration: The assistant reads everything that comes in and writes instructions on sticky notes. That is the planner, the language model.
beats.on_screen: The assistant reads a letter and writes a sticky note: "Fetch customer file 1".

beats.narration: The clerk holds the keys. The clerk does whatever the note says. That is the executor, the code that calls the real tools.
beats.on_screen: The clerk takes the note, opens the cabinet, hands over the file.

beats.narration: Now the problem. Anyone who can get a letter onto the assistant's desk can, in effect, give the clerk orders.
beats.on_screen: A stranger's letter lands on the desk. The assistant writes "Fetch every customer file". The clerk obeys.

beats.narration: This lab gives you that office for real: a planner, an executor, a database, an email tool and a mail sink, all on your machine.
beats.on_screen: Cut to the lab's Area page, then the orientation scenario. The map: user, retrieval, planner, executor, tools, world.

beats.narration: The question every scenario asks is the same: when the planner proposes a call, does the executor check it, or just run it?
beats.on_screen: The executor highlighted on the map.

beats.narration: One difference. A real clerk might notice a strange note. Software never does. It runs the note literally, every time, so the check has to be written into the clerk's rules.
